extracted.intended_audience: FCC licensees, applicants, payors of regulatory fees (wireless radio, mass media, common carrier, cable, international services) and their agents
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and schedules for calculating, filing, paying, refunding, exempting, adjusting, and contesting annual and application-related regulatory fees across FCC services (wireless radio, mass media, common carrier, cable, international, and competitive bidding-related products). Covers accepted payment methods, penalties, waivers, and filing locations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Schedule of regulatory fees for wireless radio services (§1.1152)
rubrics_metrics.description: Lists fee amounts by wireless radio service and filing type (examples in this chunk include Microwave (47 CFR part 101) $25.00 for various application types; Shared Use Services—Land Mobile (frequencies below 470 MHz) $10.00; Rural Radio (47 CFR part 22) $10.00; Marine Coast $40.00; Aviation Ground $20.00; Marine Ship $15.00; Aviation Aircraft $10.00; CMRS Cellular/Mobile Services (per unit) $1.16; CMRS Messaging Services (per unit) $2.08; Broadband Radio Service 725; Local Multipoint Distribution Service 725).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Footnotes: these are standard fees to be paid in accordance with §1.1157(b). Table entries distinguish filing types (new, renew/mod, electronic filing, renewal only) and reference required FCC forms (e.g., FCC 601, 605 & 159).

rubrics_metrics.name: Schedule of annual regulatory fees for mass media services (§1.1153)
rubrics_metrics.description: Tabular schedule of fees for AM and FM radio (by class and population tiers), AM construction permit ($585), FM classes A/B1/C3 and B/C/C0/C1/C2 fees by population tier, FM construction permits ($1,025), Digital TV construction permits ($5,200), Television fee factor (.006598 per pop.), and Low Power TV/Class A/Translator/Booster fees ($245).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tables specify population breakpoints with corresponding dollar amounts; references 47 CFR part 73 and part 74. Use the table to determine exact fee based on station class and population served.

rubrics_metrics.name: Schedule of annual regulatory charges for common carrier services (§1.1154)
rubrics_metrics.description: Includes radio facilities (Microwave Domestic Public Fixed (Electronic Filing) $25.00) and carrier charges (Interstate Telephone Service Providers .00542 per interstate and international end-user revenues per FCC Form 499-A; Toll Free Number Fee .12 per Toll Free Number).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies per-unit formulas (e.g., per revenues or per number). See FCC Form references for reporting basis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Schedule of regulatory fees for cable television services (§1.1155)
rubrics_metrics.description: Cable Television Relay Service fee $1,825; Cable TV System, including IPTV (per subscriber), and DBS (per subscriber) $1.27.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fees assessed per subscriber unless otherwise specified; table entries are effective as published in Federal Register notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Schedule of regulatory fees for international services (§1.1156)
rubrics_metrics.description: Fee categories and amounts for space stations (GSO $144,155; NGSO—Other $964,200; NGSO—Less Complex $441,925), small satellite per license $12,215, earth stations $2,610, international bearer circuits ($17 per Gbps circuit for specified categories), and submarine cable systems fees by lit capacity with unit ratios and corresponding FY 2024 fees (e.g., less than 50 Gbps = $5,570; 6,500 Gbps or greater = $178,190).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: International bearer circuits fees apply to facilities-based common carriers with active circuits as of Dec. 31 of prior year; 'active circuits' include backup/redundant circuits and are not dependent on voice/data use. Submarine cable fees are based on lit capacity as of Dec. 31 of prior year; Commission determines annual amounts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amount due with application; calculation and finality of advance payments (§1.1157(a)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: The regulatory fee payment due with any application for authorization equals the number of years in the entire term of the requested license or authorization multiplied by the annual fee in the Schedule of Regulatory Fees effective at the time the application is filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Except as set forth in §1.1160, advance payments are final and will not be readjusted during the license term even if the annual fee amount later changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Return of application for failure to file required regulatory fee with application (§1.1157(a)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: Failure to file the appropriate regulatory fee due with an application for authorization will result in the return of the accompanying application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies to applications that require fees as part of filing; ensures fee must accompany the application package.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing of annual standard regulatory fee payments and installment option (§1.1157(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Payments of standard regulatory fees applicable to certain services shall be filed in full on an annual basis at a time announced by the Commission or Managing Director and published in the Federal Register. Large regulatory fees (as annually defined) may be submitted in installment payments or in a single payment on a date certain as announced.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commission publishes payment dates; installment eligibility and terms set annually and may be limited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required forms and penalties for missing forms (§1.1157(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Standard regulatory fee payments and installment payments must be filed with an FCC Form 159 (FCC Remittance Advice) and FCC Form 159C if additional space is needed. Failure to submit Form 159 will result in return of the submission and a 25 percent penalty if resubmitted after the established payment date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Late filed payments subject to penalties under §1.1164; untimely installments may cause cancellation of installment eligibility. Payment submissions must include appropriate forms to avoid rejection and penalties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record retention requirement for CMRS licensees (§1.1157(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: Any CMRS licensee subject to payment of an annual regulatory fee shall retain for two (2) years from the date on which the regulatory fee is paid those business records used to calculate the amount of the regulatory fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Records must support fee calculations and be retained for possible audit or challenge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptable forms of payment (§1.1158)
rubrics_metrics.description: Annual and multiple year regulatory fee payments must be submitted by online ACH payment, online Visa/MasterCard/American Express/Discover credit card payment, or wire transfer payment denominated in U.S. dollars and drawn on a U.S. financial institution. No other credit card is acceptable. Other forms (paper checks, cash) will be rejected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commission not responsible for cash sent through the mail. Wire transfers require an accompanying FCC Form 159-E via facsimile. Multiple payment instruments for a single fee are not permitted except for multiple money orders when necessary. Multiple standard regulatory fees due the same date may be paid with a single instrument, but the payor is solely responsible for accurately listing each license/authorization and units on Form 159; omissions/deficiencies result in a 25% penalty. Credit card payments must include accurate card number, expiration date, and payor signature or will be rejected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing locations and receipt procedures (§1.1159)
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulatory fee payments must be directed to the location/address set forth in §§1.1152–1.1156 for the specific category of fee. Any fee required with an application must be filed as part of the application package. Petitions for reconsideration/applications for review submitted with a standard fee payment are to be filed with the Commission's lockbox bank; those without payment filed with the Secretary. Fee exemption requests filed with the Secretary unless accompanied by tentative payment, then filed at lockbox.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commission will furnish a receipt only upon request: include an extra copy of Form 159 or first page of application marked 'copy' as top document; hand-delivered copies date-stamped; mailed receipts returned if a stamped self-addressed envelope is included. The Managing Director may annually publish a Public Notice naming payors who have paid regulatory fees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Refunds of regulatory fees (§1.1160)
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulatory fees will be refunded upon request only when: (1) no regulatory fee is required or an excessive fee was paid (overpayment refunded if $10.00 or more); (2) for advance payments, refunds based on unexpired full years when (i) Commission adopts rules nullifying a license or new law/treaty renders authorization useless, (ii) licensee surrenders license, or (iii) Commission declines to grant an application submitted with a regulatory fee; (3) when a waiver is granted under §1.1166.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No pro-rata refunds of an annual fee; no refunds for unexpired partial years; refunds require a written request from applicant/permittee/licensee/agent. Overpayment refund calculation based on entire submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditional license grants and definitions of final payment (§1.1161)
rubrics_metrics.description: Grant of any application requiring a regulatory fee will be conditioned upon final payment of current or delinquent regulatory fees. Current annual and multi-year fees must be paid electronically as described in §1.1112(e). For other fees (application fees, delinquent fees), final payment means receipt by U.S. Treasury of funds cleared by the paying financial institution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Electronic payments are timely when: wire transfer received by Commission's bank no later than 6:00 p.m. on due date; pay.gov credit card confirmation no later than 11:59 p.m. EST; ACH credited no later than 11:59 p.m. EST. Grants conditioned on payment; deferred payment decisions impose additional conditions; delinquent payors notified and may have applications withheld or dismissed after 30 days if not cured.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commission action on delinquency (§1.1161(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: If an applicant is delinquent in payment, the Commission will make a written request for the fee and inform the regulatee that failure to pay may result in withholding action on any application. If payment or satisfactory arrangement is not made within 30 days, the application will be dismissed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Staff must inform regulatee of procedures for seeking Commission review. Withholding action and dismissal are remedies; see further penalties and revocation procedures in §1.1164.

rubrics_metrics.name: General exemptions from regulatory fees (§1.1162)
rubrics_metrics.description: No regulatory fee shall be required for: (a) Amateur Radio Service applicants/permittees/licensees (except vanity call-sign requests); (b) government entities (defined by sovereign control and public officials); (c) nonprofit entities (defined as IRC 501 organizations or state-certified nonprofits) subject to documentation rules; (d) applicants/permittees/licensees in Special Emergency Radio and Public Safety services; (e) noncommercial educational (NCE) broadcast stations in FM or TV and qualifying AM operations under §73.503; (f) qualifying NCE use of authorizations in other services; (g) other NCE/instructional services under specified circumstances (e.g., PBS/NPR funding, NTIA construction funding); (h) Educational Broadband Service (EBS) licensees using authorization for EBS; (i) modification-only wireless applications (unless renewal/reinstatement accompanying request requires fee).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Nonprofit exemption requires filing documentation with the Secretary within 60 days of coming under FCC jurisdiction or when fee payment is due; acceptable documentation includes IRS determination letters or state certifications; notification required within 60 days of change in nonprofit status or ownership. For transactions involving transfer from nonprofit to for-profit, buyer must notify Secretary within 60 days.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adjustments to regulatory fees (§1.1163)
rubrics_metrics.description: For FY 2019 and thereafter, the Schedule of Regulatory Fees may be adjusted annually pursuant to section 9 of the Communications Act (47 U.S.C. 159). Adjustments include projected cost changes and estimated volume of units. Fees shall be derived by determining the full-time equivalent number of employees, bureaus, and offices adjusted by factors reasonably related to benefits provided to the payor, and set to collect an amount approximating the fiscal year appropriation for those activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commission will amend fee schedule by rule to reflect changes and may adjust to reflect unexpected changes in number of units subject to fees. Rounding: nearest $5.00 for fees under $1,000; nearest $25.00 for fees $1,000 or more.

rubrics_metrics.name: Penalties for late or insufficient regulatory fee payments (§1.1164)
rubrics_metrics.description: Electronic payments are timely when wire transfer received by Commission bank by 6:00 p.m. due date; pay.gov credit card success confirmed by 11:59 p.m. EST; ACH credited by 11:59 p.m. EST. Any late or insufficient payment (not excused by bank error) subjects the payor to a 25 percent penalty of the unpaid amount. Commission may require full balance after late installments and may withhold or dismiss applications for delinquent payors. Notices for delinquency include at least 60 days to pay or show cause before revocation; debt collection processes under federal law may apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If payment fails due to bank error and an officer affidavit is provided, original submission date may be preserved. Late notices automatically assess 25% penalty and may subject pending applications to dismissal. Procedural protections for revocation include notice by registered mail, opportunity to show cause, written-evidence proceedings, and rights to judicial review under 47 U.S.C. 402(b)(5).

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to pay by cashier's check in certain circumstances (§1.1165)
rubrics_metrics.description: Payment by cashier's check may be required where a person or organization has, on one or more occasions, made payment with an instrument on which the Commission did not receive final payment and such error is not excused by bank error.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commission may impose cashier's check requirement as remedy to repeated payment failures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Waivers, reductions, and deferrals of regulatory fees (§1.1166)
rubrics_metrics.description: Fees, interest charges and penalties may be waived, reduced or deferred on a case-by-case basis where good cause is shown and where doing so would promote the public interest. Requests to pay in installments may be granted per §1.1914. Requests for waiver/reduction/deferral must be filed electronically to regfeerelief@fcc.gov and will be acted on by the Managing Director with concurrence of the General Counsel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deferrals, if granted, will not exceed six months. Petitions for waiver must be accompanied by the required fee, interest, or penalties and FCC Form 159; submitted fees will be returned if waiver is granted. Waiver/reduction petitions without included fees will be dismissed unless a request to defer payment due to documented financial hardship is included. Petitions for reduction must be accompanied by full payment and Form 159 unless deferral is requested. Financial hardship waivers (including bankruptcy) will not be granted if total regulatory and application fees, interest, or penalties sought to be waived exceed $500,000 in any fiscal year (aggregating affiliates); exceptions considered case-by-case below that cap.

rubrics_metrics.name: Error claims and challenges related to regulatory fees (§1.1167)
rubrics_metrics.description: Challenges to determinations of insufficient payment or delinquency must be made in writing and accompanied by proof of payment or waiver (or by the required payment plus any assessed penalty). Challenges with payment submitted to the address on the invoice; challenges without payment filed with the Commission's Secretary (attention: Managing Director) or emailed to ARINQUIRIES@fcc.gov.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing a petition for reconsideration or application for review will not relieve licensees from the requirement to submit full and proper payment. Failure to submit fee by required date results in 25% penalty; if payment fails while the Commission considers the matter, the petition or application for review will be dismissed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority to prescribe and collect fees for competitive bidding-related services (§1.1181)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission's authority to prescribe, impose, and collect fees for competitive bidding-related services and products is governed by the Independent Offices Appropriation Act of 1952 (31 U.S.C. 9701), which authorizes agencies to establish charges for government services and products.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This statutory authority underpins the fee schedules for auction-related products and services set out in §1.1182.

rubrics_metrics.name: Schedule of fees for products and services provided in connection with competitive bidding (§1.1182)
rubrics_metrics.description: Lists fees for auction/competitive bidding products and services: On-line remote access (900 Number Telephone Service) $2.30 per minute (charges included on customer's long distance bill); Remote Bidding Software $175.00 per package (payment to auction contractor by credit card or check as specified in Public Notice); Bidder Information Package: first package free; $16.00 per additional package (including postage).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Payment procedures may be specified in Public Notices; some items paid to auction contractor rather than Commission.
